title: Derby day
goal: Follow a derby-day story full of particles, and use them in a message of your own.

intro.text: Two brothers, two teams, one derby. This story mixes every small word of the unit. Read it aloud: these words carry the tone of a sentence, and they sound right only with the voice that goes with them.

vocab.en: half (of a match: ilk yarı, ikinci yarı)
whistle (ıslık çalmak: to whistle; to boo)

exercises.title: Derbi günü
exercises.passage:
Pazar günü derbi vardı. Ben Fenerbahçeliyim, kardeşim Can ise Galatasaraylı. Sabahtan beri evde gergin bir hava vardı. Annem “Sakın kavga etmeyin, maç sadece bir oyun!” dedi.

Maç Kadıköy'deydi. Stadyuma o kadar erken gittik ki tribünler daha boştu. Ama yarım saat sonra stadyum doldu bile. Taraftarlar şarkı söyleyip duruyordu; ben bile sesimi kaybettim.

İlk golü Galatasaray attı. Can ayağa fırladı, ben donakaldım. Hani sabah “Bugün kazanacağız!” diyordum ya, biraz utandım. Ama ikinci yarıda biz de bir gol attık, hem de son dakikada! Maç berabere bitti.

Eve dönerken Can güldü: “İşte futbol böyle bir şey. Kimse kazanmadı, bari ikimiz de mutlu olalım.” Annem bizi kapıda karşıladı: “Kim kazandı?” “Kimse!” dedik, ikimiz de gülerek.
exercises.translation: On Sunday there was a derby. I'm a Fenerbahçe fan; my brother Can supports Galatasaray. Since the morning the atmosphere at home had been tense. My mother said: “Don't you dare fight, a match is only a game!” The match was in Kadıköy. We went to the stadium so early that the stands were still empty. But half an hour later the stadium was already full. The fans kept singing; even I lost my voice. Galatasaray scored the first goal. Can leapt to his feet, and I froze. You remember how I'd been saying “We're going to win today!” that morning? I felt a bit embarrassed. But in the second half we scored too, and in the last minute at that! The match ended in a draw. On the way home Can laughed: “That's football for you. Nobody won, so let's at least both be happy.” My mother met us at the door: “Who won?” “Nobody!” we said, both laughing.

questions.q: What was the stadium like when the brothers arrived?
options: Still empty: they had come very early
questions.explain: *O kadar erken gittik ki tribünler daha boştu*: **so early that…**

questions.q: Why was the narrator embarrassed when Galatasaray scored?
options: He had been boasting that his team would win
He had shouted at the referee
questions.explain: *Hani sabah “Bugün kazanacağız!” diyordum ya*: *hani … ya* recalls what he had been saying.

questions.q: What does *hem de son dakikada* add?
options: The equalizer came in the last minute, which made it even better
Both teams scored in the last minute
The match lasted one more minute
questions.explain: *Hem de* adds a stronger point: **and in the last minute at that**.

exercises.text: Stadyum o kadar gürültülüydü ___ ben ___ sesimi kaybettim.
exercises.en: The stadium was so noisy that even I lost my voice.

accept: ki

reject.why: After *o kadar …*, the result opens with *ki*.

exercises.explain: *O kadar gürültülüydü ki*: so … that. *Ben bile*: **even I**.

exercises.prompt: Don't you dare fight, it's only a game!
accept: Sakın kavga etmeyin, bu sadece bir oyun!
Sakın kavga etmeyin sadece bir oyun!
Sakın kavga etme sadece bir oyun!
Sakın kavga etme bu sadece bir oyun!
Sakın kavga etmeyin yalnızca bir oyun!
Sakın kavga etmeyin bu yalnızca bir oyun!
Sakın kavga etme yalnızca bir oyun!
Sakın kavga etme bu yalnızca bir oyun!

reject.answer: Sakın kavga edin, bu sadece bir oyun!

exercises.explain: *Sakın* + the negative imperative *etmeyin* (or *etme* to one person).

exercises.en: The stadium was already full within half an hour.

accept: Weren't we going to win today?
Weren't we supposed to win today?
I thought we were [going|supposed] to win today?
Weren't we meant to win today?
Futbol işte böyle bir şey.

exercises.question: Complete: *Kazanamıyorsak ___ berabere kalalım.* (If we can't win, let's at least draw.)

why.1: *Hele* urges or stresses **especially**; it doesn't settle for less.
why.2: *Bile* is **even**, which doesn't fit a second-best wish.

exercises.tr: Ya bu akşam ya yarın maçı izleriz.
exercises.en: We'll watch the match either tonight or tomorrow.
options: Ya bu akşam ya yarın maçı izleriz.
Bu akşam ya da yarın maçı izledik.

accept: Hakem bile güldü.

reject.why: *Hakem de güldü* is **the referee laughed too**. **Even** is *bile*.
*Bile* follows the word it stresses: *hakem bile*.

exercises.explain: *Hakem bile*: *bile* after the word it stresses.

context.en: I wonder if there are any tickets left for the match.
I don't know, but let's at least have a look.

exercises.question: What does Can suggest?
options: They should buy the tickets now.

why.1: *Bari* means they should try, not give up.
why.2: He doesn't know if there are tickets; he only suggests looking.

exercises.explain: *Bari bir bakalım*: **let's at least have a look**, the next best thing to knowing.

accept: He came, and early at that!
She came, and early at that!
[He|She] came, and early too!
He came, and [what's more|on top of that], he came early!
She came, and [what's more|on top of that], she came early!
He came, and he was early too!
She came, and she was early too!

exercises.task: Write a short message (three or four sentences) inviting a friend to watch a big match with you. Use at least three of *bile*, *ki*, *ya*, *hani*, *işte*, *sakın* and *bari*.
models: Cumartesi derbi var, biliyorsun ya. Bizim evde izleyelim, annem börek bile yapacak. Sakın geç kalma, maç sekizde başlıyor. Gelemiyorsan bari haber ver.
Hani maçı birlikte izleyecektik? Biletler o kadar pahalı ki stadyuma gidemiyoruz, ama kafede büyük bir ekran var. İşte orada buluşalım!
checklist: At least three particles, each in its place: *bile* after the word it stresses, *sakın* before a negative imperative
*Ya* after a statement as a reminder, or *ya … ya* for a choice
The optative or the imperative for the invitation: *izleyelim*, *gel*, *buluşalım*
